   183→    def set_speed(self, factor: float) -> StateChange:
   184→        self._time.factor = factor
   185→        return {"type": "speed_change", "factor": factor}
   186→
   187→    # ── Canonical decision close ─────────────────────────────────────────
   188→
   189→    async def close_decision(
   190→        self,
   191→        decision_id: str,
   192→        selected_option_ids: list[str],
   193→        target_system_selections: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   194→    ) -> list[StateChange]:
   195→        """Single canonical path for closing a decision.
   196→
   197→        Handles: validate → close → score → resolve forced cards →
   198→        record plays → system effects (with optional target overrides) →
   199→        advance turn → auto-complete.
   200→
   201→        Args:
   202→            target_system_selections: map of option_id → system_id for
   203→                options with targets_system=True. Pass None on timeout
   204→                to skip target-system effects.
   205→
   206→        Raises ValueError if decision missing/closed, max_selections
   207→        violated, or a required target system selection is missing/invalid.
   208→        """
   209→        pt = self._time.play_time_ms
   210→
   211→        decision = self._decisions.get_decision(decision_id)
   212→        if decision is None or decision.status != "open":
   213→            raise ValueError(f"Decision {decision_id} not found or already closed")
   214→
   215→        template = self.find_decision_template(decision_id)
   216→
   217→        # Validate max_selections
   218→        if template and template.max_selections is not None:
   219→            if len(selected_option_ids) > template.max_selections:
   220→                raise ValueError(
   221→                    f"Decision {decision_id} allows at most "
   222→                    f"{template.max_selections} selections, "
   223→                    f"got {len(selected_option_ids)}"
   224→                )
   225→
   226→        # 1. Close
   227→        close_change = self._decisions.close_decision(
   228→            decision_id, current_pt_ms=pt, selected_option_ids=selected_option_ids,
   229→        )
   230→        if not close_change:
   231→            raise ValueError(f"Decision {decision_id} not found or already closed")
   232→        changes: list[StateChange] = [close_change]
   233→
   234→        # 2. Score (forced cards handled inside game mode)
   235→        selected_opts = [o for o in decision.options if o["id"] in selected_option_ids]
   236→        forced_ids = template.forced_option_ids if template else []
   237→        score_changes = self._config.game_mode.on_decision_closed_v2(
   238→            decision_id,
   239→            selected_opts,
   240→            decision.options,
   241→            forced_option_ids=forced_ids or None,
   242→            turn_stress_delta=template.stress_delta if template else 0,
   243→        )
   244→        changes.extend(score_changes)
   245→
   246→        # 3. Resolve effective options (selected + auto-added forced cards)
   247→        effective_opts = self._resolve_effective_options(
   248→            selected_opts, decision.options, forced_ids,
   249→        )
   250→
   251→        # 4. Record plays + system effects on effective options
   252→        self.record_option_plays(effective_opts)
   253→        changes.extend(self._apply_system_effects(effective_opts, target_system_selections))
   254→
   255→        # 5. Advance to next turn (or auto-complete if exhausted)
   256→        advance = await self._advance_to_next_turn(decision_id, pt)
   257→        changes.extend(advance)
   258→
   259→        # 6. Auto-resume for GM mode
   260→        if self._config.game_mode.requires_gm():
   261→            if not self._decisions.get_open_decisions():
   262→                changes.append(await self.resume())
   263→
   264→        return changes
   265→
   266→    def _resolve_effective_options(
   267→        self,
   268→        selected: list[DecisionOptionSnapshot],
   269→        all_options: list[DecisionOptionSnapshot],
   270→        forced_ids: list[str],
   271→    ) -> list[DecisionOptionSnapshot]:
   272→        """Return selected + auto-added forced card options."""
   273→        selected_ids = {o["id"] for o in selected}
   274→        effective = list(selected)
   275→        for fid in forced_ids or []:
   276→            if fid not in selected_ids:
   277→                forced_opt = next((o for o in all_options if o["id"] == fid), None)
   278→                if forced_opt is not None:
   279→                    effective.append(forced_opt)
   280→        return effective
   281→
   282→    async def _advance_to_next_turn(
   283→        self, closed_decision_id: str, pt: float,
   284→    ) -> list[StateChange]:
   285→        """Advance to next decision in sequence, or auto-complete if exhausted."""
   286→        advance = self.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, closed_decision_id)
   287→        if advance:
   288→            return advance
   289→        # Sequence exhausted — auto-complete if still running
   290→        if (
   291→            self._config.game_mode.get_next_decision_id(closed_decision_id) is None
   292→            and self._phase == EnginePhase.RUNNING
   293→        ):
   294→            try:
   295→                return [await self.complete()]
   296→            except EngineStateError:
   297→                pass  # Another path already completed
   298→        return []
   299→
   300→    # ── Canonical event trigger ────────────────────────────────────────
   301→
   302→    def trigger_event(self, event_id: str) -> list[StateChange]:
   303→        """Single canonical path for triggering an event.
   304→
   305→        Handles: force-trigger → event system effects →
   306→        event domain effects → open decision (if applicable).
   307→
   308→        Raises ValueError if event missing or not triggerable.
   309→        """
   310→        pt = self._time.play_time_ms
   311→        event = self._events.events.get(event_id)
   312→        if not event:
   313→            raise ValueError(f"Event {event_id} not found")
   314→        event_change = self._events.force_trigger(event_id, pt)
   315→        if not event_change:
   316→            raise ValueError(f"Event {event_id} not triggerable")
   317→        changes: list[StateChange] = [event_change]
   318→        # Apply system effects
   319→        if event.system_effects:
   320→            changes.extend(self._apply_event_system_effects(event.system_effects))
   321→        # Apply domain effects
   322→        if event.domain_effects:
   323→            changes.extend(self._apply_event_domain_effects(event.domain_effects))
   324→        # Open decision if applicable
   325→        changes.extend(self._handle_decision_events([event_change], pt))
   326→        return changes
   327→
   328→    async def tick(self) -> list[StateChange]:
   329→        """Advance time, check triggers, return state changes."""
   330→        changes: list[StateChange] = []
   331→        self._time.tick()
   332→        pt = self._time.play_time_ms
   333→
   334→        event_changes = self._events.tick(pt)
   335→        changes.extend(event_changes)
   336→
   337→        # Apply system effects from events that just started
   338→        # (force-triggered events are handled in force_trigger_next_decision)
   339→        for change in event_changes:
   340→            if change.get("action") == "started":
   341→                event = self._events.events.get(change["event_id"])
   342→                if event and event.system_effects:
   343→                    changes.extend(self._apply_event_system_effects(event.system_effects))
   344→                if event and event.domain_effects:
   345→                    changes.extend(self._apply_event_domain_effects(event.domain_effects))
   346→
   347→        decision_changes = self._handle_decision_events(event_changes, pt)
   348→        changes.extend(decision_changes)
   349→
   350→        completed_events = {
   351→            eid
   352→            for eid, ev in self._events.events.items()
   353→            if ev.lifecycle == EventLifecycle.COMPLETED
   354→        }
   355→
   356→        for change in event_changes:
   357→            if change.get("action") == "completed":
   358→                event_id = change["event_id"]
   359→                issue_changes = self._issues.activate_by_event(event_id, pt)
   360→                changes.extend(issue_changes)
   361→
   362→        issue_changes = self._issues.tick(pt, completed_events)
   363→        changes.extend(issue_changes)
   364→
   365→        if changes and self._on_state_change:
   366→            await self._on_state_change(changes)
   367→        return changes
   368→
   369→    def snapshot(self) -> EngineSnapshot:
   370→        """Full state snapshot for client sync."""
   371→        return EngineSnapshot(
   372→            exercise_id=self._config.exercise_id,
   373→            title=self._config.title,
   374→            phase=self._phase.value,
   375→            time=self._time.snapshot(),
   376→            events=self._events.snapshot(),
   377→            issues=self._issues.snapshot(),
   378→            decisions=self._decisions.snapshot(),
   379→            score=self._config.game_mode.snapshot(),
   380→            systems=self._systems.snapshot(),
   381→            warfare_domains=self._warfare_domains.snapshot(),
   382→        )
   383→
   384→    def _handle_decision_events(
   385→        self,
   386→        event_changes: list[StateChange],
   387→        pt: float,
   388→    ) -> list[DecisionOpened]:
   389→        changes: list[DecisionOpened] = []
   390→        for change in event_changes:
   391→            if change.get("action") not in ("started", "force_triggered"):
   392→                continue
   393→            event_id = change["event_id"]
   394→            event = self._events.events.get(event_id)
   395→            if event is None or event.event_type != EventType.DECISION:
   396→                continue
   397→            # Skip if there's already an open decision (prevent tick-loop pile-up)
   398→            if self._decisions.get_open_decisions():
   399→                continue
   400→            t = self.find_decision_template(event_id)
   401→            template_timeout = t.timeout_ms if t else 0.0
   402→            # If template has no timeout, use game mode's stress-based timer
   403→            timeout_ms = template_timeout or self._config.game_mode.get_decision_time_ms(0)
   404→            changes.append(
   405→                self._decisions.open_decision(
   406→                    id=t.id if t else event_id,
   407→                    event_id=event_id,
   408→                    issue_id=t.issue_id if t else None,
   409→                    title=t.title if t else event.title,
   410→                    description=t.description if t else event.description,
   411→                    question_type=t.question_type if t else "free_text",
   412→                    options=t.options if t else [],
   413→                    completion_mode=t.completion_mode if t else "first_response",
   414→                    target_roles=t.target_roles if t else [],
   415→                    timeout_ms=timeout_ms,
   416→                    max_selections=t.max_selections if t else None,
   417→                    current_pt_ms=pt,
   418→                )
   419→            )
   420→            if self._config.game_mode.should_pause_on_decision():
   421→                self._phase = EnginePhase.PAUSED
   422→                self._time.pause()
   423→                self._stop_tick_loop()
   424→            if timeout_ms > 0:
   425→                self._start_timeout_monitor()
   426→        return changes
   427→
   428→    def find_decision_template(self, event_id: str) -> DecisionTemplate | None:
   429→        return next((dt for dt in self._config.decision_templates if dt.id == event_id), None)
   430→
   431→    def force_trigger_next_decision(
   432→        self, pt: float, closed_decision_id: str = "",
   433→    ) -> list[StateChange]:
   434→        """Force-trigger the next event in the game mode's decision sequence.
   435→
   436→        Called after closing a decision (player submission or timeout).
   437→        Returns event_change + decision_opened state changes, or [] if
   438→        the sequence is exhausted or the next event doesn't exist.
   439→        """
   440→        next_id = self._config.game_mode.get_next_decision_id(closed_decision_id)
   441→        if not next_id:
   442→            return []
   443→        event = self._events.events.get(next_id)
   444→        if not event:
   445→            return []
   446→        event_change = self._events.force_trigger(next_id, pt)
   447→        if not event_change:
   448→            return []
   449→        changes: list[StateChange] = [event_change]
   450→        # Apply system effects from force-triggered event
   451→        if event and event.system_effects:
   452→            changes.extend(self._apply_event_system_effects(event.system_effects))
   453→        # Apply domain effects from force-triggered event
   454→        if event and event.domain_effects:
   455→            changes.extend(self._apply_event_domain_effects(event.domain_effects))
   456→        changes.extend(self._handle_decision_events([event_change], pt))
   457→        return changes
   458→
   459→    def _start_tick_loop(self) -> None:
   460→        if self._tick_task is None or self._tick_task.done():
   461→            self._tick_task = asyncio.create_task(self._tick_loop())
   462→
   463→    def _stop_tick_loop(self) -> None:
   464→        if self._tick_task and not self._tick_task.done():
   465→            self._tick_task.cancel()
   466→            self._tick_task = None
   467→
   468→    async def _tick_loop(self) -> None:
   469→        try:
   470→            while True:
   471→                await self.tick()
   472→                await asyncio.sleep(TICK_INTERVAL_S)
   473→        except asyncio.CancelledError:
   474→            pass
   475→
   476→    def _start_timeout_monitor(self) -> None:
   477→        if not self._timeout_task or self._timeout_task.done():
   478→            self._timeout_task = asyncio.create_task(self._timeout_loop())
   479→
   480→    def _stop_timeout_monitor(self) -> None:
   481→        if self._timeout_task and not self._timeout_task.done():
   482→            self._timeout_task.cancel()
   483→            self._timeout_task = None
   484→
   485→    def _is_timed_out(self, decision: object) -> bool:
   486→        """Check if a decision has exceeded its wall-clock timeout."""
   487→        now_ms = _time_mod.monotonic() * 1000
   488→        return (
   489→            decision.timeout_ms > 0
   490→            and (now_ms - decision.opened_at_rt_ms) >= decision.timeout_ms
   491→        )
   492→
   493→    def _select_timeout_option(self, decision: object) -> str | None:
   494→        """Pick the auto-submit option for a timed-out decision."""
   495→        available = [o for o in decision.options if not self.is_option_exhausted(o)]
   496→        return self._config.game_mode.on_decision_timeout(
   497→            decision.id,
   498→            available or decision.options,
   499→        )
   500→
   501→    async def _timeout_loop(self) -> None:
   502→        """Monitor open decisions for wall-clock timeout expiry."""
   503→        try:
   504→            while self._decisions.get_open_decisions():
   505→                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
   506→                for d in list(self._decisions.get_open_decisions()):
   507→                    if not self._is_timed_out(d):
   508→                        continue
   509→                    auto_id = self._select_timeout_option(d)
   510→                    selected = [auto_id] if auto_id else []
   511→                    changes = await self.close_decision(d.id, selected)
   512→                    if changes and self._on_state_change:
   513→                        await self._on_state_change(changes)
   514→                if not self._decisions.get_open_decisions():
   515→                    break
   516→        except asyncio.CancelledError:
   517→            pass
   518→
   519→    def _apply_system_effects(
   520→        self,
   521→        selected_options: list[DecisionOptionSnapshot],
   522→        target_system_selections: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   523→    ) -> list[SystemStateChange]:
   524→        """Apply system_effects from selected decision options via SystemManager."""
   525→        out: list[SystemStateChange] = []
   526→        for opt in selected_options:
   527→            effects = opt["system_effects"]
   528→            if opt["targets_system"]:
   529→                sel = (target_system_selections or {}).get(opt["id"])
   530→                if sel is None:
   531→                    if target_system_selections is not None:
   532→                        raise ValueError(
   533→                            f"Option {opt['id']} requires a target system selection"
   534→                        )
   535→                    # No selections at all (e.g. timeout) — skip effect
   536→                    continue
   537→                if sel not in self._systems.systems:
   538→                    raise ValueError(f"Target system '{sel}' not found")
   539→                effects = [
   540→                    SystemEffect(
   541→                        system_id=sel,
   542→                        operational_state=fx["operational_state"],
   543→                        power_state=fx["power_state"],
   544→                        set_all_power=fx["set_all_power"],
   545→                    )
   546→                    for fx in effects
   547→                ]
   548→            out.extend(self._apply_effects_list(effects))
   549→        return out
   550→
   551→    def _apply_event_system_effects(
   552→        self, effects: list[SystemEffect],
   553→    ) -> list[SystemStateChange]:
   554→        """Apply system_effects from an event (inject) via SystemManager."""
   555→        return self._apply_effects_list(effects)
   556→
   557→    def _apply_event_domain_effects(
   558→        self, effects: list[DomainEffect],
   559→    ) -> list[WarfareDomainChange]:
   560→        """Apply domain_effects from an event (inject) via WarfareDomainManager."""
   561→        out: list[WarfareDomainChange] = []
   562→        for fx in effects:
   563→            if c := self._warfare_domains.set_threat_level(fx["domain_id"], fx["threat_level"]):
   564→                out.append(c)
   565→        return out
   566→
   567→    def _apply_effects_list(
   568→        self, effects: list[SystemEffect],
   569→    ) -> list[SystemStateChange]:
   570→        """Shared logic for applying a list of SystemEffect dicts."""
   571→        out: list[SystemStateChange] = []
   572→        for fx in effects:
   573→            if fx.get("set_all_power"):
   574→                on = fx["power_state"] if fx["power_state"] is not None else True
   575→                out.extend(self._systems.set_all_power(on))
   576→                continue
   577→            if fx["power_state"] is not None:
   578→                if c := self._systems.set_power(fx["system_id"], fx["power_state"]):
   579→                    out.append(c)
   580→            if fx["operational_state"] is not None:
   581→                if c := self._systems.set_operational(fx["system_id"], fx["operational_state"]):
   582→                    out.append(c)
   583→        return out
   584→
   585→    def _phase_change(self, action: str) -> PhaseChange:
   586→        return {
   587→            "type": "phase_change",
   588→            "action": action,
   589→            "phase": self._phase.value,
   590→            "time": self._time.snapshot(),
   591→        }
   592→

1→"""Pydantic models defining the structured JSON stored in tfc_scenarios.content.
     2→
     3→These models validate scenario data authored by the GM and serve as the
     4→bridge between the scenario editor and the exercise engine.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator
    10→
    11→from core.game_mode_constants import GM_CLASSIC, GM_SIMPLE_COLLABORATIVE
    12→
    13→
    14→class SystemEffectDef(BaseModel):
    15→    """A system state change triggered by selecting a decision option or event start."""
    16→
    17→    system_id: str
    18→    operational_state: str | None = None  # "green" | "yellow" | "red"
    19→    power_state: bool | None = None
    20→    set_all_power: bool = False  # General Quarters: power all systems ON
    21→
    22→
    23→class DomainEffectDef(BaseModel):
    24→    """A warfare domain threat-level change triggered by an event."""
    25→
    26→    domain_id: str
    27→    threat_level: str  # "green" | "yellow" | "red"
    28→
    29→
    30→class DecisionOptionDef(BaseModel):
    31→    """A single selectable option within a decision template."""
    32→
    33→    id: str
    34→    label: str
    35→    score: float = 0.0
    36→    stress_delta: int = 0
    37→    system_effects: list[SystemEffectDef] = []
    38→    targets_system: bool = False
    39→    max_plays: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)  # 0 = unlimited, 1+ = explicit limit
    40→
    41→
    42→class DecisionTemplateDef(BaseModel):
    43→    """Template for a decision that players must make during an exercise."""
    44→
    45→    id: str
    46→    title: str
    47→    description: str = ""
    48→    issue_id: str  # linked issue
    49→    question_type: str  # single_choice, multi_choice, free_text, scale
    50→    options: list[DecisionOptionDef] = []
    51→    completion_mode: str = "first_response"
    52→    timeout_ms: float = 0  # 0 = no timeout
    53→    target_roles: list[str] = []
    54→    forced_option_ids: list[str] = []
    55→    max_selections: int | None = None  # None = unlimited
    56→    stress_delta: int = 0  # turn-level stress applied regardless of card choice
    57→
    58→
    59→class ScenarioEventDef(BaseModel):
    60→    """Definition of an inject (event) within a scenario. Domain term: 'inject'."""
    61→
    62→    id: str
    63→    title: str
    64→    description: str = ""
    65→    event_type: str  # informational, operational, decision
    66→    scheduled_pt_ms: float  # when to trigger in play time
    67→    duration_ms: float | None = None  # auto-complete after duration
    68→    dependencies: list[str] = []  # event IDs that must complete first
    69→    triggered_issues: list[str] = []  # issue IDs activated on completion
    70→    target_roles: list[str] = []  # empty = visible to all roles
    71→    role_descriptions: dict[str, str] = {}  # per-role description overrides
    72→    system_effects: list[SystemEffectDef] = []  # system state changes on event start
    73→    domain_effects: list[DomainEffectDef] = []  # warfare domain changes on event start
    74→
    75→
    76→class ScenarioIssueDef(BaseModel):
    77→    """Definition of a defect (issue) within a scenario. Domain term: 'defect'."""
    78→
    79→    id: str
    80→    title: str
    81→    description: str = ""
    82→    trigger_mode: str  # time-based, event-based, manual
    83→    trigger_time_pt_ms: float | None = None
    84→    trigger_event_id: str | None = None
    85→    auto_resolve_ms: float = 0  # 0 = no auto-resolve
    86→
    87→
    88→class ScenarioPhaseDef(BaseModel):
    89→    """Definition of a phase grouping events within a scenario."""
    90→
    91→    id: str
    92→    title: str
    93→    description: str = ""
    94→    duration_ms: float | None = None  # auto-advance after duration
    95→    events: list[str] = []  # event IDs in this phase
    96→
    97→
    98→class SystemStateDef(BaseModel):
    99→    """Initial or expected system state in scenario definition."""
   100→
   101→    system_id: str
   102→    label: str = ""
   103→    category: str = "system"  # "system" | "weapon"
   104→    operational_state: str | None = None  # "green"|"yellow"|"red"
   105→    power_state: bool | None = None
   106→
   107→
   108→class WarfareDomainDef(BaseModel):
   109→    """Initial warfare domain definition in scenario."""
   110→
   111→    domain_id: str
   112→    label: str = ""
   113→    initial_threat_level: str = "green"
   114→
   115→
   116→class TurnDefinition(BaseModel):
   117→    """Groups injects and a decision template into a turn."""
   118→
   119→    turn_index: int
   120→    title: str = ""
   121→    facilitator_prompt: str | None = None
   122→    has_decisions: bool = True
   123→    inject_ids: list[str] = []
   124→    decision_template_id: str | None = None
   125→    base_stress_delta: int = 0
   126→
   127→
   128→class RoleDef(BaseModel):
   129→    """Definition of a participant role within a scenario."""
   130→
   131→    id: str
   132→    label: str
   133→    player_type: str = "advisor"  # "advisor" or "decision_maker"
   134→
   135→
   136→class ScenarioContent(BaseModel):
   137→    """Top-level scenario definition validated against this schema.
   138→
   139→    This is the structured JSON stored in the ``tfc_scenarios.content``
   140→    column. The GM authors this via the scenario editor; the engine
   141→    loader converts it into runtime objects at exercise start.
   142→    """
   143→
   144→    phases: list[ScenarioPhaseDef] = []
   145→    events: list[ScenarioEventDef] = []
   146→    issues: list[ScenarioIssueDef] = []
   147→    decision_templates: list[DecisionTemplateDef] = []
   148→    default_time_factor: float = 1.0
   149→    briefing: str = ""
   150→    objectives: list[str] = []
   151→    rules: list[str] = []
   152→    game_mode: str = GM_CLASSIC
   153→    game_mode_config: dict[str, object] = {}
   154→    decision_sequence: list[str] = []
   155→    roles: list[RoleDef] = []
   156→    turns: list[TurnDefinition] = []
   157→    initial_system_states: list[SystemStateDef] = []
   158→    initial_warfare_domains: list[WarfareDomainDef] = []
   159→    score_tier_thresholds: dict[str, float] = {}  # {"lo": 0.33, "mid": 0.66}
   160→
   161→    @model_validator(mode="after")
   162→    def validate_roles(self) -> ScenarioContent:
   163→        """Enforce that every scenario defines roles appropriate for its game mode."""
   164→        if not self.roles:
   165→            raise ValueError("Scenario must define at least one role in 'roles'.")
   166→        role_ids = {r.id for r in self.roles}
   167→        player_types = {r.player_type for r in self.roles}
   168→        if "decision_maker" not in player_types:
   169→            raise ValueError(
   170→                "Scenario must have at least one role with player_type='decision_maker'."
   171→            )
   172→        if self.game_mode == GM_SIMPLE_COLLABORATIVE and len(self.roles) < 2:
   173→            raise ValueError(
   174→                "Simple collaborative scenarios require at least 2 playable "
   175→                f"roles, but only {len(self.roles)} defined."
   176→            )
   177→        for dt in self.decision_templates:
   178→            for rid in dt.target_roles:
   179→                if rid not in role_ids:
   180→                    raise ValueError(
   181→                        f"Decision template '{dt.id}' targets unknown "
   182→                        f"role '{rid}'. Defined roles: {sorted(role_ids)}."
   183→                    )
   184→        for evt in self.events:
   185→            for rid in evt.target_roles:
   186→                if rid not in role_ids:
   187→                    raise ValueError(
   188→                        f"Event '{evt.id}' targets unknown "
   189→                        f"role '{rid}'. Defined roles: {sorted(role_ids)}."
   190→                    )
   191→            for rid in evt.role_descriptions:
   192→                if rid not in role_ids:
   193→                    raise ValueError(
   194→                        f"Event '{evt.id}' has role_description for unknown "
   195→                        f"role '{rid}'. Defined roles: {sorted(role_ids)}."
   196→                    )
   197→        return self
   198→

1→"""REST endpoints for waiting room participant management.
     2→
     3→Allows participants to join, leave, and change roles before an exercise
     4→starts. Mutations broadcast updates via the existing WebSocket connection
     5→manager so all connected clients see changes in real time.
     6→
     7→When the exercise is linked to a scenario with roles, the router enforces:
     8→- unique role assignment (no two participants hold the same role)
     9→- max player capacity (derived from the number of defined roles)
    10→"""
    11→
    12→from __future__ import annotations
    13→
    14→from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
    15→
    16→from core.dependencies import get_exercise_service, get_scenario_service
    17→from features.exercise.adapters.connection_manager import connection_manager
    18→from features.exercise.exercise_service import ExerciseService
    19→from features.scenario.scenario_content import ScenarioContent
    20→from features.scenario.scenario_service import ScenarioService
    21→from features.waiting_room.waiting_room_schema import (
    22→    JoinRequest,
    23→    ParticipantResponse,
    24→    UpdateRoleRequest,
    25→    WaitingRoomResponse,
    26→)
    27→from features.waiting_room.waiting_room_store import waiting_room_store
    28→
    29→router = APIRouter(
    30→    prefix="/api/exercises/{exercise_id}/waiting-room",
    31→    tags=["waiting-room"],
    32→)
    33→
    34→
    35→def _participants_payload(exercise_id: int) -> dict:
    36→    """Build the broadcast payload for waiting room updates."""
    37→    participants = waiting_room_store.list_participants(exercise_id)
    38→    return {
    39→        "type": "waiting_room_update",
    40→        "exercise_id": exercise_id,
    41→        "participants": [p.to_dict() for p in participants],
    42→    }
    43→
    44→
    45→async def _get_scenario_roles(
    46→    exercise_id: int,
    47→    exercise_service: ExerciseService,
    48→    scenario_service: ScenarioService,
    49→) -> list[dict] | None:
    50→    """Return scenario roles for the exercise, or None if no scenario."""
    51→    exercise = await exercise_service.get_exercise(exercise_id)
    52→    if exercise.scenario_id is None:
    53→        return None
    54→    scenario = await scenario_service.get_scenario(exercise.scenario_id)

content.text:
Both agents launched. Now for #172:

The short answer is **no** — it wouldn't require rewriting scenarios. The current coupling works by ID convention: event `evt-t1` implicitly maps to decision template `evt-t1`. Adding an explicit `decision_template_id` field to events would be:

1. **Backwards-compatible** — if the field is `null`, fall back to the current ID-matching behavior
2. **Seed update is mechanical** — add `"decision_template_id": "evt-t1"` to each of the 15 decision events in `silent_wake.json` (the value equals the existing event ID, so it's just making the implicit explicit)
3. **No scenario structure change** — events stay events, decision templates stay templates, the relationship just gets a proper foreign key instead of a naming convention

The real question is whether you want to go further — e.g. allowing one event to trigger *multiple* decisions, or a decision template to be reusable across events. That would be a bigger design change. But the issue as filed (add `decision_template_ids` to events) is a straightforward schema addition with zero behavioral change for existing scenarios.

What's the concern that's preoccupying you about it?

#!/bin/bash
# Pre-push hook: regenerate API client (if possible), show diff, then lint.
# Push proceeds regardless of generation failure, but lint must pass.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
GENERATED_DIR="$ROOT/frontend/src/app/shared/api/generated"

echo "═══ pre-push: attempting API client generation ═══"

# Step 1: Try to extract OpenAPI spec from running backend
if cd "$ROOT/backend" && python -c "import json; from main import create_app; print(json.dumps(create_app().openapi(), indent=2))" > "$ROOT/shared/openapi.json" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "✓ OpenAPI spec extracted"

  # Step 2: Regenerate frontend client
  if bash "$ROOT/shared/scripts/generate-frontend.sh"; then
    echo "✓ Frontend client regenerated"

    # Step 3: Show diff between regenerated and committed code
    cd "$ROOT"
    if ! git diff --quiet -- "$GENERATED_DIR"; then
      echo ""
      echo "⚠ Generated API client differs from committed version:"
      echo "────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
      git diff --stat -- "$GENERATED_DIR"
      echo ""
      git diff -- "$GENERATED_DIR"
      echo "────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
      echo "⚠ Consider committing the updated generated files."
      echo ""
    else
      echo "✓ Generated client matches committed version"
    fi
  else
    echo "⚠ Frontend client generation failed (openapi-ts error)"
  fi
else
  echo "⚠ Backend not available — skipping generation (using committed stubs)"
  git checkout -- "$ROOT/shared/openapi.json" 2>/dev/null  # restore committed version
fi

# Step 4: TFC codegen freshness (must pass to push)
echo ""
echo "═══ pre-push: checking TFC codegen freshness ═══"
if ! bash "$ROOT/apps/tfc/codegen/check-freshness.sh"; then
  echo "✗ TFC codegen freshness check failed"
  exit 1
fi

# Step 5: Lint (must pass to push)
echo ""
echo "═══ pre-push: running linters ═══"

for backend in apps/main/backend apps/tfc/backend; do
  name="$(basename "$(dirname "$backend")")/$(basename "$backend")"
  echo "→ $name: ruff check"
  if ! (cd "$ROOT/$backend" && ruff check .); then
    echo "✗ $name ruff check failed"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "→ $name: ruff format --check"
  if ! (cd "$ROOT/$backend" && ruff format --check .); then
    echo "✗ $name ruff format failed"
    exit 1
  fi
done

for fe in apps/main/frontend apps/tfc/frontend; do
  name="$(basename "$(dirname "$fe")")/$(basename "$fe")"
  echo "→ $name: eslint"

#!/bin/bash
# Pre-push hook: regenerate API client (if possible), show diff, then lint.
# Push proceeds regardless of generation failure, but lint must pass.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
GENERATED_DIR="$ROOT/frontend/src/app/shared/api/generated"

echo "═══ pre-push: attempting API client generation ═══"

# Step 1: Try to extract OpenAPI spec from running backend
if cd "$ROOT/backend" && python -c "import json; from main import create_app; print(json.dumps(create_app().openapi(), indent=2))" > "$ROOT/shared/openapi.json" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "✓ OpenAPI spec extracted"

  # Step 2: Regenerate frontend client
  if bash "$ROOT/shared/scripts/generate-frontend.sh"; then
    echo "✓ Frontend client regenerated"

    # Step 3: Show diff between regenerated and committed code
    cd "$ROOT"
    if ! git diff --quiet -- "$GENERATED_DIR"; then
      echo ""
      echo "⚠ Generated API client differs from committed version:"
      echo "────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
      git diff --stat -- "$GENERATED_DIR"
      echo ""
      git diff -- "$GENERATED_DIR"
      echo "────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
      echo "⚠ Consider committing the updated generated files."
      echo ""
    else
      echo "✓ Generated client matches committed version"
    fi
  else
    echo "⚠ Frontend client generation failed (openapi-ts error)"
  fi
else
  echo "⚠ Backend not available — skipping generation (using committed stubs)"
  git checkout -- "$ROOT/shared/openapi.json" 2>/dev/null  # restore committed version
fi

# Step 4: TFC codegen freshness (must pass to push)
echo ""
echo "═══ pre-push: checking TFC codegen freshness ═══"
if ! bash "$ROOT/apps/tfc/codegen/check-freshness.sh"; then
  echo "✗ TFC codegen freshness check failed"
  exit 1
fi

# Step 5: Lint (must pass to push)
echo ""
echo "═══ pre-push: running linters ═══"

for backend in apps/main/backend apps/tfc/backend; do
  name="$(basename "$(dirname "$backend")")/$(basename "$backend")"
  ruff_bin="$ROOT/$backend/.venv/bin/ruff"
  if [ ! -x "$ruff_bin" ]; then
    echo "⚠ $name: ruff not found in venv, skipping"
    continue
  fi
  echo "→ $name: ruff check"
  if ! (cd "$ROOT/$backend" && "$ruff_bin" check .); then
    echo "✗ $name ruff check failed"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "→ $name: ruff format --check"
  if ! (cd "$ROOT/$backend" && "$ruff_bin" format --check .); then
    echo "✗ $name ruff format failed"
    exit 1
  fi
done

for fe in apps/main/frontend apps/tfc/frontend; do
  name="$(basename "$(dirname "$fe")")/$(basename "$fe")"
  echo "→ $name: eslint"
  if ! (cd "$ROOT/$fe" && npx eslint 'src/**/*.ts'); then
    echo "✗ $name eslint failed"
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Step 6: TypeScript type check (must pass to push)
echo ""
echo "═══ pre-push: running TypeScript checks ═══"

echo "→ tfc/frontend: tsc (app + spec)"
if ! (cd "$ROOT/apps/tfc/frontend" && npm run lint:tsc:all); then
  echo "✗ TFC frontend type check failed"
  exit 1
fi

# Step 7: Prettier (must pass to push)
echo ""
echo "═══ pre-push: checking formatting ═══"

for fe in apps/main/frontend apps/tfc/frontend; do
  name="$(basename "$(dirname "$fe")")/$(basename "$fe")"
  echo "→ $name: prettier"
  if ! (cd "$ROOT/$fe" && npx prettier --check 'src/**/*.{ts,html,css,json}'); then
    echo "✗ $name prettier check failed — run: npx prettier --write 'src/**/*.{ts,html,css,json}'"
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Step 8: TFC build (catches template errors like @else if breakage)
echo ""
echo "═══ pre-push: verifying TFC build ═══"

echo "→ tfc/frontend: ng build"
if ! (cd "$ROOT/apps/tfc/frontend" && npm run build); then
  echo "✗ TFC frontend build failed"
  exit 1
fi

echo ""
echo "✓ All checks passed"

"""Tests for ExerciseEngine.close_decision() — canonical decision close path.

Verifies that the engine's public close_decision method handles the full
lifecycle: close → score → forced cards → system effects → advance → complete.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from engine.engine_config import DecisionTemplate, EngineConfig, ScenarioContext
from engine.event_scheduler import EventType, ScheduledEvent
from engine.exercise_engine import EnginePhase, ExerciseEngine
from engine.game_modes.simple_collaborative import SimpleCollaborativeMode
from engine.state_changes import DecisionOptionSnapshot, SystemEffect
from engine.system_manager import SystemState


def _option(
    id: str,
    *,
    score: float = 0.0,
    stress_delta: int = 0,
    system_effects: list[SystemEffect] | None = None,
    targets_system: bool = False,
    max_plays: int = 0,
) -> DecisionOptionSnapshot:
    return DecisionOptionSnapshot(
        id=id,
        label=f"Option {id}",
        score=score,
        stress_delta=stress_delta,
        system_effects=system_effects or [],
        targets_system=targets_system,
        max_plays=max_plays,
        role=None,
    )


def _build_engine(
    decision_templates: list[DecisionTemplate],
    initial_systems: list[SystemState] | None = None,
) -> ExerciseEngine:
    """Build a running engine with events matching each decision template."""
    events = [
        ScheduledEvent(
            id=dt.id,
            title=f"Event {dt.id}",
            description="",
            event_type=EventType.DECISION,
            scheduled_pt_ms=999_999,
            dependencies=[decision_templates[i - 1].id] if i > 0 else [],
        )
        for i, dt in enumerate(decision_templates)
    ]
    mode = SimpleCollaborativeMode(
        decision_sequence=[dt.id for dt in decision_templates],
        base_decision_time_ms=300_000,
    )
    config = EngineConfig(
        exercise_id=1,
        title="Test",
        events=events,
        decision_templates=decision_templates,
        context=ScenarioContext(),
        initial_system_states=initial_systems or [],
        game_mode=mode,
    )
    return ExerciseEngine(config)


def _single_turn_template(
    tid: str = "d1",
    options: list[DecisionOptionSnapshot] | None = None,
    max_selections: int | None = 1,
    forced_option_ids: list[str] | None = None,
) -> DecisionTemplate:
    return DecisionTemplate(
        id=tid,
        title=f"Decision {tid}",
        description="",
        issue_id="i1",
        question_type="single_choice",
        options=options or [_option("good", score=10.0), _option("bad", score=0.0)],
        completion_mode="consensus",
        target_roles=["co"],
        max_selections=max_selections,
        forced_option_ids=forced_option_ids or [],
    )


class TestCloseDecisionBasic:
    """Engine.close_decision returns all state changes for the full lifecycle."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_decision_closed_and_score(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        types = [c["type"] for c in changes]
        assert "decision_closed" in types
        assert "score_change" in types

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_single_turn_auto_completes(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        assert engine.phase == EnginePhase.COMPLETED
        phase_changes = [c for c in changes if c["type"] == "phase_change"]
        assert any(c["phase"] == "completed" for c in phase_changes)

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_multi_turn_does_not_complete_on_first(self) -> None:
        dt1 = _single_turn_template("d1")
        dt2 = _single_turn_template("d2")
        engine = _build_engine([dt1, dt2])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        assert engine.phase == EnginePhase.RUNNING
        # Should have advanced to d2
        types = [c["type"] for c in changes]
        assert "decision_opened" in types

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_raises_on_invalid_decision_id(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()

        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            await engine.close_decision("nonexistent", ["good"])

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_raises_on_already_closed(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_raises_on_too_many_selections(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template(max_selections=1)
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good", "bad"])


class TestCloseDecisionSystemEffects:
    """System effects from selected options are applied via close_decision."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_applies_system_effects(self) -> None:
        opts = [
            _option(
                "shutdown",
                score=1.0,
                system_effects=[
                    SystemEffect(
                        system_id="nav",
                        power_state=False,
                        operational_state="red",
                        set_all_power=False,
                    ),
                ],
            ),
            _option("keep", score=0.0),
        ]
        dt = _single_turn_template(options=opts)
        systems = [SystemState(system_id="nav", label="NAV", power=True, operational="green")]
        engine = _build_engine([dt], initial_systems=systems)
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["shutdown"])

        assert engine.system_manager.systems["nav"].power is False
        assert engine.system_manager.systems["nav"].operational == "red"
        sys_changes = [c for c in changes if c.get("type") == "system_state_change"]
        assert len(sys_changes) >= 1


class TestCloseDecisionForcedCards:
    """Forced cards are auto-added and their effects applied."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_forced_card_system_effects_applied(self) -> None:
        opts = [
            _option("normal", score=5.0),
            _option(
                "forced",
                score=-2.0,
                system_effects=[
                    SystemEffect(
                        system_id="comms",
                        power_state=None,
                        operational_state="yellow",
                        set_all_power=False,
                    ),
                ],
            ),
        ]
        dt = _single_turn_template(
            options=opts,
            forced_option_ids=["forced"],
        )
        systems = [
            SystemState(system_id="comms", label="COMMS", power=True, operational="green"),
        ]
        engine = _build_engine([dt], initial_systems=systems)
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        # Player selects "normal" only — "forced" should be auto-added
        await engine.close_decision("d1", ["normal"])

        # Forced card's system effect must be applied
        assert engine.system_manager.systems["comms"].operational == "yellow"
        # Score should include both normal (5) + forced (-2) = 3
        assert engine.game_mode.total_score == 3.0


class TestCloseDecisionTargetSystem:

    @pytest.mark.asyncio

class TestBriefingPhaseEngine:
    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_start_enters_briefing_phase(self) -> None:
        """engine.start() should transition SETUP → BRIEFING, not RUNNING."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        result = await engine.start()
        assert engine.phase == EnginePhase.BRIEFING
        assert result["phase"] == "briefing"
        assert result["action"] == "started"

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_start_does_not_start_tick_loop(self) -> None:
        """In BRIEFING phase, the tick loop must NOT be running."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        await engine.start()
        # Tick task should not have been created
        assert engine._tick_task is None or engine._tick_task.done()

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_time_does_not_advance_in_briefing(self) -> None:
        """Play time should remain at 0 while in BRIEFING."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        await engine.start()
        assert engine.time_manager.play_time_ms == 0.0

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_begin_transitions_to_running(self) -> None:
        """engine.begin() should transition BRIEFING → RUNNING and start the clock."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        await engine.start()
        with patch("engine.time_manager._now_ms", return_value=0.0):
            result = await engine.begin()
        assert engine.phase == EnginePhase.RUNNING
        assert result["phase"] == "running"
        assert result["action"] == "begun"
        engine._stop_tick_loop()

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_begin_rejects_from_setup(self) -> None:
        """Cannot begin() from SETUP — must start() first."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        with pytest.raises(EngineStateError):
            await engine.begin()

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_begin_rejects_from_running(self) -> None:
        """Cannot begin() if already RUNNING."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        await engine.start()
        with patch("engine.time_manager._now_ms", return_value=0.0):
            await engine.begin()
        with pytest.raises(EngineStateError):
            await engine.begin()
        engine._stop_tick_loop()

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_begin_rejects_from_completed(self) -> None:
        """Cannot begin() from COMPLETED."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        await engine.start()
        with patch("engine.time_manager._now_ms", return_value=0.0):
            await engine.begin()
            await engine.complete()
        with pytest.raises(EngineStateError):
            await engine.begin()

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_snapshot_shows_briefing_phase(self) -> None:
        """Snapshot should reflect the BRIEFING phase."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        await engine.start()
        snap = engine.snapshot()
        assert snap["phase"] == "briefing"

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_context_available_in_briefing(self) -> None:
        """Engine context (briefing text) should be available in BRIEFING phase."""
        ctx = ScenarioContext(
            briefing="You are the crew of a Frigate...",
            objectives=["Maintain mission tempo"],
        )
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config(context=ctx))
        await engine.start()
        assert engine.config.context.briefing == "You are the crew of a Frigate..."
        assert engine.config.context.objectives == ["Maintain mission tempo"]

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_reset_from_briefing_returns_to_setup(self) -> None:
        """Reset from BRIEFING should go back to SETUP."""
        engine = ExerciseEngine(_config())
        await engine.start()
        result = await engine.reset()
        assert engine.phase == EnginePhase.SETUP
        assert result["phase"] == "setup"

"""Tests for ExerciseEngine.close_decision() — canonical decision close path.

Verifies that the engine's public close_decision method handles the full
lifecycle: close → score → forced cards → system effects → advance → complete.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from engine.engine_config import DecisionTemplate, EngineConfig, ScenarioContext
from engine.event_scheduler import EventType, ScheduledEvent
from engine.exercise_engine import EnginePhase, ExerciseEngine
from engine.game_modes.simple_collaborative import SimpleCollaborativeMode
from engine.state_changes import DecisionOptionSnapshot, SystemEffect
from engine.system_manager import SystemState


def _option(
    id: str,
    *,
    score: float = 0.0,
    stress_delta: int = 0,
    system_effects: list[SystemEffect] | None = None,
    targets_system: bool = False,
    max_plays: int = 0,
) -> DecisionOptionSnapshot:
    return DecisionOptionSnapshot(
        id=id,
        label=f"Option {id}",
        score=score,
        stress_delta=stress_delta,
        system_effects=system_effects or [],
        targets_system=targets_system,
        max_plays=max_plays,
        role=None,
    )


def _build_engine(
    decision_templates: list[DecisionTemplate],
    initial_systems: list[SystemState] | None = None,
) -> ExerciseEngine:
    """Build a running engine with events matching each decision template."""
    events = [
        ScheduledEvent(
            id=dt.id,
            title=f"Event {dt.id}",
            description="",
            event_type=EventType.DECISION,
            scheduled_pt_ms=999_999,
            dependencies=[decision_templates[i - 1].id] if i > 0 else [],
        )
        for i, dt in enumerate(decision_templates)
    ]
    mode = SimpleCollaborativeMode(
        decision_sequence=[dt.id for dt in decision_templates],
        base_decision_time_ms=300_000,
    )
    config = EngineConfig(
        exercise_id=1,
        title="Test",
        events=events,
        decision_templates=decision_templates,
        context=ScenarioContext(),
        initial_system_states=initial_systems or [],
        game_mode=mode,
    )
    return ExerciseEngine(config)


def _single_turn_template(
    tid: str = "d1",
    options: list[DecisionOptionSnapshot] | None = None,
    max_selections: int | None = 1,
    forced_option_ids: list[str] | None = None,
) -> DecisionTemplate:
    return DecisionTemplate(
        id=tid,
        title=f"Decision {tid}",
        description="",
        issue_id="i1",
        question_type="single_choice",
        options=options or [_option("good", score=10.0), _option("bad", score=0.0)],
        completion_mode="consensus",
        target_roles=["co"],
        max_selections=max_selections,
        forced_option_ids=forced_option_ids or [],
    )


class TestCloseDecisionBasic:
    """Engine.close_decision returns all state changes for the full lifecycle."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_decision_closed_and_score(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        types = [c["type"] for c in changes]
        assert "decision_closed" in types
        assert "score_change" in types

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_single_turn_auto_completes(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        assert engine.phase == EnginePhase.COMPLETED
        phase_changes = [c for c in changes if c["type"] == "phase_change"]
        assert any(c["phase"] == "completed" for c in phase_changes)

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_multi_turn_does_not_complete_on_first(self) -> None:
        dt1 = _single_turn_template("d1")
        dt2 = _single_turn_template("d2")
        engine = _build_engine([dt1, dt2])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        assert engine.phase == EnginePhase.RUNNING
        # Should have advanced to d2
        types = [c["type"] for c in changes]
        assert "decision_opened" in types

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_raises_on_invalid_decision_id(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not found"):
            await engine.close_decision("nonexistent", ["good"])

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_raises_on_already_closed(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not open"):
            await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_raises_on_too_many_selections(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template(max_selections=1)
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="exceeds max_selections"):
            await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good", "bad"])


class TestCloseDecisionSystemEffects:
    """System effects from selected options are applied via close_decision."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_applies_system_effects(self) -> None:
        opts = [
            _option(
                "shutdown",
                score=1.0,
                system_effects=[
                    SystemEffect(
                        system_id="nav",
                        power_state=False,
                        operational_state="red",
                        set_all_power=False,
                    ),
                ],
            ),
            _option("keep", score=0.0),
        ]
        dt = _single_turn_template(options=opts)
        systems = [SystemState(system_id="nav", label="NAV", power=True, operational="green")]
        engine = _build_engine([dt], initial_systems=systems)
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["shutdown"])

        assert engine.system_manager.systems["nav"].power is False
        assert engine.system_manager.systems["nav"].operational == "red"
        sys_changes = [c for c in changes if c.get("type") == "system_state_change"]
        assert len(sys_changes) >= 1


class TestCloseDecisionForcedCards:
    """Forced cards are auto-added and their effects applied."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_forced_card_system_effects_applied(self) -> None:
        opts = [
            _option("normal", score=5.0),
            _option(
                "forced",
                score=-2.0,
                system_effects=[
                    SystemEffect(
                        system_id="comms",
                        power_state=None,
                        operational_state="yellow",
                        set_all_power=False,
                    ),
                ],
            ),
        ]
        dt = _single_turn_template(
            options=opts,
            forced_option_ids=["forced"],
        )
        systems = [
            SystemState(system_id="comms", label="COMMS", power=True, operational="green"),
        ]
        engine = _build_engine([dt], initial_systems=systems)
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

"""Tests for ExerciseEngine.close_decision() — canonical decision close path.

Verifies that the engine's public close_decision method handles the full
lifecycle: close → score → forced cards → system effects → advance → complete.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from engine.engine_config import DecisionTemplate, EngineConfig, ScenarioContext
from engine.event_scheduler import EventType, ScheduledEvent
from engine.exercise_engine import EnginePhase, ExerciseEngine
from engine.game_modes.simple_collaborative import SimpleCollaborativeMode
from engine.state_changes import DecisionOptionSnapshot, SystemEffect
from engine.system_manager import SystemState


def _option(
    id: str,
    *,
    score: float = 0.0,
    stress_delta: int = 0,
    system_effects: list[SystemEffect] | None = None,
    targets_system: bool = False,
    max_plays: int = 0,
) -> DecisionOptionSnapshot:
    return DecisionOptionSnapshot(
        id=id,
        label=f"Option {id}",
        score=score,
        stress_delta=stress_delta,
        system_effects=system_effects or [],
        targets_system=targets_system,
        max_plays=max_plays,
        role=None,
    )


def _build_engine(
    decision_templates: list[DecisionTemplate],
    initial_systems: list[SystemState] | None = None,
) -> ExerciseEngine:
    """Build a running engine with events matching each decision template."""
    events = [
        ScheduledEvent(
            id=dt.id,
            title=f"Event {dt.id}",
            description="",
            event_type=EventType.DECISION,
            scheduled_pt_ms=999_999,
            dependencies=[decision_templates[i - 1].id] if i > 0 else [],
        )
        for i, dt in enumerate(decision_templates)
    ]
    mode = SimpleCollaborativeMode(
        decision_sequence=[dt.id for dt in decision_templates],
        base_decision_time_ms=300_000,
    )
    config = EngineConfig(
        exercise_id=1,
        title="Test",
        events=events,
        decision_templates=decision_templates,
        context=ScenarioContext(),
        initial_system_states=initial_systems or [],
        game_mode=mode,
    )
    return ExerciseEngine(config)


def _single_turn_template(
    tid: str = "d1",
    options: list[DecisionOptionSnapshot] | None = None,
    max_selections: int | None = 1,
    forced_option_ids: list[str] | None = None,
) -> DecisionTemplate:
    return DecisionTemplate(
        id=tid,
        title=f"Decision {tid}",
        description="",
        issue_id="i1",
        question_type="single_choice",
        options=options or [_option("good", score=10.0), _option("bad", score=0.0)],
        completion_mode="consensus",
        target_roles=["co"],
        max_selections=max_selections,
        forced_option_ids=forced_option_ids or [],
    )


class TestCloseDecisionBasic:
    """Engine.close_decision returns all state changes for the full lifecycle."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_decision_closed_and_score(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        types = [c["type"] for c in changes]
        assert "decision_closed" in types
        assert "score_change" in types

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_single_turn_auto_completes(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        assert engine.phase == EnginePhase.COMPLETED
        phase_changes = [c for c in changes if c["type"] == "phase_change"]
        assert any(c["phase"] == "completed" for c in phase_changes)

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_multi_turn_does_not_complete_on_first(self) -> None:
        dt1 = _single_turn_template("d1")

        await engine.start()

        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        changes = await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        # Should have advanced to d2
        types = [c["type"] for c in changes]
        assert "decision_opened" in types

    async def test_raises_on_invalid_decision_id(self) -> None:
        dt = _single_turn_template()

        dt = _single_turn_template()
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="already closed"):
            await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good"])

    @pytest.mark.asyncio

        dt = _single_turn_template(max_selections=1)
        engine = _build_engine([dt])
        await engine.start()
        await engine.begin()
        pt = engine.time_manager.play_time_ms
        engine.force_trigger_next_decision(pt, "")

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="exceeds max_selections"):
            await engine.close_decision("d1", ["good", "bad"])

# Spec-Driven Development Workflow

## Overview

**No code without a spec. No implementation without a plan.**

This skill enforces the winning workflow pattern from industry consensus:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. SPECIFY  │  PRD → Design doc → Acceptance criteria     │
├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  2. PLAN     │  Architecture → Task breakdown (<200 LOC)   │
├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  3. IMPLEMENT│  One task at a time, commit per task        │
├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  4. VALIDATE │  Tests → Review → Human approval            │
└──────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       ↑                                              │
       └──────────── Retrospective ◄──────────────────┘
```

## When to Use

**Always, for any non-trivial work:**
- New features
- Significant refactors
- Bug fixes that touch multiple files
- Anything that could take >30 minutes

**Exceptions (ask first):**
- One-line typo fixes
- Documentation-only changes
- Emergency hotfixes (but retrospect afterward!)

## The Phases

### Phase 1: SPECIFY

**Goal:** Lock intent before implementation.

Create or identify a specification:

```markdown
## Feature: [Name]

### Problem Statement
[What problem are we solving? Why does it matter?]

### User Story
As a [user type], I want to [action] so that [benefit].

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given [context], when [action], then [result]
- [ ] Given [context], when [action], then [result]
- [ ] [Edge case handled]
- [ ] [Error case handled]

### Non-Goals (Out of Scope)
- [What we're explicitly NOT doing]

### Dependencies
- [What must exist before this can work]
```

**Checklist:**
- [ ] Problem is clearly stated
- [ ] Acceptance criteria are testable
- [ ] Non-goals prevent scope creep
- [ ] User has approved the spec

**DO NOT PROCEED until spec is approved.**

### Phase 2: PLAN

**Goal:** Break down into small, testable tasks.

```markdown
## Implementation Plan

### Architecture Decision
[Which approach and why]

### File Changes
1. `path/to/file.ts` - [what changes]
2. `path/to/other.ts` - [what changes]

### Task Breakdown
Each task should be:
- ≤200 lines of code change
- Independently testable
- One commit per task

#### Task 1: [Name]
- Files: [list]
- Changes: [description]
- Test: [how to verify]

#### Task 2: [Name]
...
```

**Checklist:**
- [ ] Each task is ≤200 LOC
- [ ] Tasks have clear boundaries
- [ ] Order respects dependencies
- [ ] Each task can be tested independently
- [ ] Plan is added to TodoWrite or Beads

**Create beads/todos for each task before implementing.**

### Phase 3: IMPLEMENT

**Goal:** Execute one task at a time with TDD.

For EACH task:

```
1. Write failing test first (TDD)
2. Implement minimal code to pass
3. Refactor if needed (stay green)
4. Run all tests
5. Commit with descriptive message
6. Mark task complete
7. Move to next task
```

**Rules:**
- One task at a time, no parallelism
- One commit per task
- Test must fail before code exists
- Never skip the test phase
- Mark bead/todo complete immediately

**Commit message format:**
```
feat(scope): brief description

- Detail of change
- Another detail

Refs: beads-xxx / task-123
```

### Phase 4: VALIDATE

**Goal:** Ensure quality before declaring done.

```markdown
## Validation Checklist

### Automated Checks
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] TypeScript/lint passes
- [ ] Build succeeds

### Manual Verification
- [ ] Feature works as specified
- [ ] Edge cases handled
- [ ] Error states handled

### Code Review
- [ ] No security vulnerabilities
- [ ] No performance issues
- [ ] Code is readable
- [ ] External review (Codex/Copilot/human)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All criteria from spec are met
- [ ] User has approved the implementation
```

**If ANY check fails, return to IMPLEMENT phase.**

## Quick Commands

Use these within the skill:

| Phase | Command | Action |
|-------|---------|--------|
| SPECIFY | `/spec [feature]` | Create specification template |
| PLAN | `/plan` | Generate task breakdown |
| IMPLEMENT | `/next-task` | Get next task from list |
| VALIDATE | `/validate` | Run validation checklist |

## Phase Transitions

```
SPECIFY → PLAN:    User approves spec
PLAN → IMPLEMENT:  Tasks in TodoWrite/Beads
IMPLEMENT → VALIDATE: All tasks complete
VALIDATE → DONE:   All checks pass + user approval
VALIDATE → IMPLEMENT: Fixes needed
```

## Anti-Patterns to Reject

| Request | Response |
|---------|----------|
| "Just make it work" | "Let me create a quick spec first to align on requirements." |
| "Skip the plan, it's simple" | "Even simple features benefit from a 2-minute task breakdown." |
| "Add this while you're at it" | "That's scope creep. Let me add it as a separate task/bead." |
| "We'll test later" | "TDD is faster. Let me write the test first." |
| "Ship it, tests can wait" | "Untested code is technical debt. Let me add minimal tests." |

## Context Preservation

At each phase transition, save state:

```markdown
## Current State - [Date/Time]
Phase: [SPECIFY|PLAN|IMPLEMENT|VALIDATE]
Feature: [name]
Spec: [location or inline]
Plan: [location or inline]
Current Task: [N of M]
Blockers: [if any]
```

This enables session resume if context is lost.

## Integration with Other Skills

- **TDD**: Mandatory during IMPLEMENT phase
- **Beads**: Track tasks as issues with dependencies
- **Retrospective**: Run after VALIDATE to improve workflow
- **Exhaustive Verification**: Use during VALIDATE phase

## The Iron Rule

```
NO CODE WITHOUT SPEC
NO IMPLEMENTATION WITHOUT PLAN
NO MERGE WITHOUT VALIDATION
```

Violating any of these is "vibe coding" and leads to inconsistent results.

---

## Feature: Weapon 2-tier state (#187)

### Problem
Weapons use binary OK / non-operational, not the 3-tier red/yellow/green traffic light. `SystemManager` currently treats all systems identically — weapons can land in "yellow" which is meaningless for them.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Weapons have 2 operational states: `"green"` (OK) and `"red"` (non-operational)
- [ ] `set_operational` on a weapon rejects `"yellow"` (returns None / no-op)
- [ ] `increment_operational` on a weapon skips yellow: red → green in one step
- [ ] Frontend renders weapons with a 2-light indicator (OK/non-op) instead of 3-light traffic light
- [ ] Existing 3-tier systems are unaffected
- [ ] Silent Wake seed data unchanged (weapons already use green/red)

### Non-Goals
- No new weapon-specific game mechanics beyond the state model
- No cascading effects (#185 is separate)
- No weapon damage levels beyond binary

"""Tests for SystemManager power and operational state management."""

from engine.system_manager import SystemManager, SystemState


def _system(
    system_id: str = "s1",
    label: str = "",
    category: str = "system",
    power: bool = False,
    operational: str = "green",
) -> SystemState:
    return SystemState(
        system_id=system_id,
        label=label or f"System {system_id}",
        category=category,
        power=power,
        operational=operational,
    )


class TestLoadSystems:
    def test_load_replaces_existing(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1"), _system("s2")])
        assert len(mgr.systems) == 2
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s3")])
        assert len(mgr.systems) == 1
        assert "s3" in mgr.systems


class TestSetPower:
    def test_power_on(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", power=False)])
        change = mgr.set_power("s1", True)
        assert change is not None
        assert change["type"] == "system_state_change"
        assert change["action"] == "power_changed"
        assert change["power"] is True
        assert mgr.systems["s1"].power is True

    def test_power_no_change_returns_none(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", power=True)])
        assert mgr.set_power("s1", True) is None

    def test_power_unknown_system_returns_none(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([])
        assert mgr.set_power("unknown", True) is None


class TestSetOperational:
    def test_set_to_yellow(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", operational="green")])
        change = mgr.set_operational("s1", "yellow")
        assert change is not None
        assert change["action"] == "operational_changed"
        assert change["operational"] == "yellow"
        assert mgr.systems["s1"].operational == "yellow"

    def test_no_change_returns_none(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", operational="red")])
        assert mgr.set_operational("s1", "red") is None

    def test_invalid_state_returns_none(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1")])
        assert mgr.set_operational("s1", "purple") is None

    def test_unknown_system_returns_none(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([])
        assert mgr.set_operational("unknown", "red") is None


class TestIncrementOperational:
    def test_red_to_yellow(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", operational="red")])
        change = mgr.increment_operational("s1")
        assert change is not None
        assert mgr.systems["s1"].operational == "yellow"

    def test_yellow_to_green(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", operational="yellow")])
        change = mgr.increment_operational("s1")
        assert change is not None
        assert mgr.systems["s1"].operational == "green"

    def test_already_green_returns_none(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", operational="green")])
        assert mgr.increment_operational("s1") is None

    def test_unknown_system_returns_none(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([])
        assert mgr.increment_operational("unknown") is None


class TestSetAllPower:
    def test_all_on(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", power=False), _system("s2", power=False)])
        changes = mgr.set_all_power(True)
        assert len(changes) == 2
        assert all(s.power is True for s in mgr.systems.values())

    def test_skips_already_on(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", power=True), _system("s2", power=False)])
        changes = mgr.set_all_power(True)
        assert len(changes) == 1
        assert changes[0]["system_id"] == "s2"

    def test_all_off(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", power=True), _system("s2", power=True)])
        changes = mgr.set_all_power(False)
        assert len(changes) == 2
        assert all(s.power is False for s in mgr.systems.values())

    def test_empty_systems(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([])
        assert mgr.set_all_power(True) == []


class TestSnapshot:
    def test_snapshot_returns_all_systems(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([_system("s1", power=True, operational="yellow")])
        snap = mgr.snapshot()
        assert len(snap) == 1
        assert snap[0]["system_id"] == "s1"
        assert snap[0]["power"] is True
        assert snap[0]["operational"] == "yellow"
        assert snap[0]["label"] == "System s1"
        assert snap[0]["category"] == "system"

    def test_empty_snapshot(self) -> None:
        mgr = SystemManager()
        mgr.load_systems([])
        assert mgr.snapshot() == []
